mechanism_builds.causal_path: Subject-specific baseline physiological variability alters the distribution of extracted features between calibration and test segments, causing conformity scores to be misaligned with the true error distribution.
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Increased baseline variability leads to decreased coverage (under-coverage) relative to the nominal level.
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Physiological signals recorded from healthy adults at rest
measurable_outcomes: Empirical coverage rate of conformal intervals
Kolmogorov‑Smirnov distance between calibration and test feature distributions
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Can be tested by stratifying calibration data by subject‑specific baselines and measuring coverage drift across held‑out segments.

mechanism_builds.causal_path: Changes in sensor characteristics (impedance, gain, interference) alter the observed signal statistics, shifting the feature distribution and biasing conformity scores, which leads to coverage drift.
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Higher impedance or noise variance reduces coverage (under‑coverage) because intervals become too narrow.
measurable_outcomes: Mean absolute error of conformity scores
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Can be tested by injecting known impedance changes (e.g., via saline) and monitoring coverage.

mechanism_builds.causal_path: Physiological state transitions change the underlying generative process of the signal, altering the relationship between features and labels, which miscalibrates conformity scores and destabilizes coverage.
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Transition to higher arousal states (e.g., exercise) increases prediction error variance, leading to under‑coverage if not accounted for.
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Laboratory polysomnography or controlled exercise protocol
measurable_outcomes: Calibration error (difference between nominal and empirical coverage)
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Can be evaluated by constructing state‑stratified calibration sets and testing on held‑out state‑specific segments.

mechanism_builds.causal_path: Positive temporal autocorrelation reduces the effective independence of observations, causing the empirical quantile of conformity scores to be underestimated, which yields prediction intervals that are too narrow and under‑cover.
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Higher ρ leads to lower coverage (under‑coverage).
measurable_outcomes: Ratio of nominal to empirical interval width
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Can be assessed using block bootstrap or subsampling to adjust for dependence.

mechanism_builds.causal_path: Mislabelled events produce anomalously large or small residuals, which shift the empirical quantile used to construct conformal intervals, biasing the intervals and causing coverage drift.
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Higher label error rate reduces coverage (under‑coverage) when errors increase residuals; direction depends on bias sign.
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Can be tested by synthetically corrupting a known fraction of labels and measuring resulting coverage.

mechanism_variables: number of rare samples in calibration (n_rare)
conformity score quantile for rare class
mechanism_builds.causal_path: When rare physiological events are under‑represented in the calibration set, the conformity score quantile is dominated by common classes, producing intervals that are too narrow for rare segments and thus under‑covering them.
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Lower p_rare leads to lower coverage for rare‑event segments (under‑coverage).
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Physiological seizure or rare arrhythmia detection
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Can be evaluated by applying importance‑weighted or stratified conformal methods and comparing coverage.

mechanism_variables: residual variance as a function of amplitude
heteroscedasticity coefficient (slope of variance vs amplitude)
mechanism_builds.causal_path: Larger signal excursions produce proportionally larger prediction errors, causing error variance to change with amplitude; this violates the constant‑variance assumption of conformity scores, leading to miscalibrated intervals.
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Higher amplitude leads to decreased coverage (under‑coverage) if variance increases with amplitude.
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Can be tested by modeling variance locally (e.g., using quantile regression) and checking whether coverage improves.

mechanism_builds.causal_path: Motion or muscle artifacts generate extreme residuals (spikes) that shift the empirical quantile of conformity scores; this can inflate intervals (over‑coverage) for clean segments and produce unstable coverage across artifact‑contaminated segments.
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Higher artifact rate increases interval width, causing overall over‑coverage but segment‑wise instability.
measurable_outcomes: Coverage stability across artifact‑free vs artifact‑contaminated segments
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Can be evaluated by adding synthetic motion artifacts at known amplitudes and measuring resulting coverage changes.

mechanism_builds.causal_path: Different preprocessing (sampling rate, filtering, segmentation) alters the distribution of extracted features, creating a mismatch between calibration and test segments that biases conformity scores and leads to coverage drift.
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Lower sampling rate or stronger low‑pass filtering reduces high‑frequency information, increasing prediction error and decreasing coverage (under‑coverage) if not corrected.
measurable_outcomes: Wasserstein distance between feature distributions across protocols
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Can be assessed by harmonizing data (e.g., resampling to a common rate) and comparing coverage before and after harmonization.

mechanism_variables: model prediction influence gain (adaptive filter coefficient)
mutual information between predictions and subsequent signal
mechanism_builds.causal_path: The model’s output alters the signal (e.g., via adaptive noise cancellation), changing the distribution of future segments relative to the calibration set; conformity scores computed from outdated statistics become miscalibrated, causing coverage drift.
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Stronger feedback influence (higher gain) produces larger distribution shifts, leading to lower coverage (under‑coverage).
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Closed‑loop neurostimulation or adaptive filtering system
Calibration set collected before feedback activation
measurable_outcomes: KL divergence between calibration and post‑feedback feature distributions
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Can be tested by disabling the feedback loop and comparing coverage with and without the loop.
